nodes.name: Telegram Trigger (Hotnews Bot)
nodes.notes: Dedicated 4th bot for this workflow -- a bot token can only have one webhook, and 'Telegram Bot' (Daily Posting), the Tistory bot, and the Blogspot bot are already each wired to their own workflow. Create a new bot via @BotFather and connect it here.

nodes.name: Fetch RSS Feed
nodes.notes: onError continues so one dead/slow feed doesn't block the other 20 -- a failed fetch just contributes zero articles that hour.

nodes.name: XML to JSON (Hotnews RSS)
nodes.notes: onError continues for the same reason as Fetch RSS Feed -- a feed that returned something non-XML (e.g. an outage HTML page) just contributes nothing.

nodes.name: Extract Recent RSS Articles
nodes.notes: ⚠️ Mode is 'Run Once for Each Item' -- VERIFY IN UI that this survives import. Also verify the parsed shape of $json.rss.channel.item against a live run -- exact XML-to-JSON field nesting can vary slightly by n8n version.

nodes.name: IF No Recent RSS Articles
nodes.notes: True (nothing published across all 21 feeds in the last 2 hours) just ends silently.

nodes.name: Claude Cluster Hot News
nodes.notes: Reuses the same Anthropic API credential account as the draft-writing call further down this workflow -- a credential is an account, not a workflow, so this isn't 'sharing' with Daily Posting. A short clustering call on titles only, far cheaper than drafting.

nodes.name: IF No Clusters Found
nodes.notes: True (Claude found no 2+ outlet story this cycle) ends silently.

nodes.name: Upsert Hotnews Candidates
nodes.notes: Shared by both collection paths (RSS+clustering above, /hotcollect backfill below). Relies on unique(article_url) to silently skip an article already stored. Writes ONLY to hotnews_candidates -- a table created solely for this workflow, never touched by Daily Posting or Blogspot.

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger (Trend History Collector)
nodes.notes: Independent Google Trends RSS fetch, solely so /hotcollect DATE has a historical keyword-by-date log (hotnews_trend_history) to search Naver News against -- deliberately NOT the Daily Posting workflow's own trending_keywords table. Only dates from whenever this starts running are backfillable.

nodes.name: Insert Hotnews Trend History
nodes.notes: Relies on unique(keyword, trend_date, region) to silently skip a keyword already logged earlier that day.

nodes.name: Get Trending Keywords For Collector
nodes.notes: Read-only against hotnews_trend_history (this workflow's own table, see 'Schedule Trigger (Trend History Collector)' above) -- never trending_keywords.

parameters.text: ={{ $('Parse Hotcollect Command').first().json.target_date }} 기준으로 hotnews_trend_history에 수집된 키워드가 없습니다.

nodes.name: Search Naver News (Hotnews Collector)
nodes.notes: display=5 so multiple 'top articles' per keyword can accumulate, not just one headline.

nodes.name: Parse Hotnews Collector Articles
nodes.notes: ⚠️ Mode is 'Run Once for Each Item' -- VERIFY IN UI that this survives import.

return [{ json: { count: items.length } }];

nodes.name: Get Unposted Hotnews Candidates
nodes.notes: Fetches all rows -- filtered to posted_at IS NULL and capped at 20 in Rank Broadcast Candidates next.

nodes.name: Insert Hotnews Broadcast Row
nodes.notes: Inserts {chat_id, items} -- the DB-generated id is re-fetched next (Supabase create responses don't reliably include it on every n8n version).

nodes.notes: VERIFY IN UI: confirm 'Limit Wait Time' toggle and the Amount field's expression mode survive import.

nodes.name: IF Broadcast Retry

nodes.name: Trigger Item Processing
nodes.notes: ⚠️ VERIFY IN UI after import -- this node's exact fields vary by n8n version. It must: (1) target THIS SAME workflow (the {{ $workflow.id }} expression self-references it -- confirm the picker accepts it, or select this workflow directly by name), (2) Mode = 'Run Once for Each Item', (3) 'Wait For Sub-Workflow Completion' turned ON -- items are processed ONE AT A TIME on purpose (see this workflow's README on why sequential, not parallel).

parameters.text: =▶️ {{ $json.count }}개 항목({{ $json.keywords }}) 처리를 순차적으로 시작했습니다. 각 항목은 뉴스 검토 승인을 거쳐 개별적으로 워드프레스 초안이 등록되며, 완료 시마다 따로 알려드립니다.

nodes.name: Get Hotnews Broadcast For Lookup
nodes.notes: Fetches all rows -- filtering to the pending one happens in the next Code node.

nodes.name: Resolve Hotnews Broadcast
nodes.notes: A GET to $execution.resumeUrl of the still-waiting broadcast execution, carrying 'selection' as a query param.

nodes.name: Execute Workflow Trigger (Item)
nodes.notes: Entry point for each selected item, fired sequentially by 'Trigger Item Processing' above (self-call, one sub-execution at a time).

nodes.name: Search Naver News
nodes.notes: sort=sim (relevance), not date -- this workflow's items can be backfilled from months/years ago, and Naver's 'date' sort only ever returns the newest matches regardless of query, which would never surface old articles at all. VERIFY IN UI: re-enter your real X-NCP-APIGW-API-KEY-ID/SECRET here after import.

nodes.name: IF News Found
nodes.notes: Moved to run directly off Parse & Split Articles's always-present single item (instead of after Insert News/Aggregate News), so the 'no recent news' branch fires reliably even when count is 0 -- previously zero articles meant Insert News/Aggregate News never ran at all, silently killing this check and the Telegram notification below.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens: 4096, tools: [{ name: "blog_draft", description: "워드프레스에 바로 등록 가능한 블로그 초안 생성", input_schema: { type: "object", properties: { title: { type: "string" }, body_html: { type: "string" }, excerpt: { type: "string" }, tags: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }, category: { type: "string", enum: ["정치", "경제", "사회", "생활/문화", "IT/과학", "연예", "스포츠", "국제", "기타", "본방사수"] }, meta_description: { type: "string" }, body_image_keywords: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" }, minItems: 2, maxItems: 2 } }, required: ["title", "body_html", "excerpt", "tags", "category", "meta_description", "body_image_keywords"] } }], tool_choice: { type: "tool", name: "blog_draft" }, messages: [{ role: "user", content: (() => { const structure = $('Pick Post Structure Variant').first().json; const base = `지금 화제인 키워드: ${$('Build News Summary').first().json.keyword} 관련 뉴스: ${$('Build News Summary').first().json.news_list} Google Trends 원본 링크: ${$('Build News Summary').first().json.trend_link} 위 내용을 참고해서 이 키워드를 자연스럽게 다루는 한국어 블로그 글을 작성해줘. 작성 지침: - 이번 글의 도입부는 반드시 다음 방식을 따라야 해: ${structure.introDirective}. '~가 화제인 이유는', '~에 대해 알아보겠습니다' 같은 상투적이고 AI스러운 문장으로는 절대 시작하지 마. - body_html의 마무리 문단은 아래 마무리 스타일 중 이 글 내용과 가장 잘 어울리는 하나를 골라서 그 방식으로 써: 1) 전망/예측형 -- 사건이 아직 진행 중이거나 결론이 안 났을 때 2) 질문형 -- 의견이 갈리는 논쟁적 사안일 때 3) 실용 조언형 -- 독자가 실제로 참고하거나 행동할 수 있는 사안일 때 4) 여운형 -- 감정적이거나 인간적인 이야기일 때 5) 재조명형 -- 사회적 파급력이 크거나 의미 있는 사안일 때 6) 아이러니형 -- 풍자적이거나 역설적인 지점이 있는 사안일 때 '관전 포인트는', '지켜봐야 할 대목이다', '귀추가 주목된다' 같은 상투적 문구는 쓰지 말고, 고른 스타일에 맞게 너만의 관점을 담아 자연스럽게 마무리해. - 뉴스 출처 인용은 마무리 문단이 아니라 본문 중 관련 있는 곳 아무 데나 자연스럽게 배치해 -- 반드시 실제 기사 URL을 href 속성 값으로 넣은 진짜 a 태그(예: 여는 태그는 a href="기사URL", 링크 텍스트는 매체명이나 기사 제목, 닫는 태그는 /a)를 써야 해. URL을 그냥 평문으로 적거나 링크 없이 언급만 하면 안 돼. 참고한 기사가 여러 개면 관련 있는 곳마다 나눠서 인용해도 좋아. - 과거 사례나 비슷한 사건과의 비교는 ${structure.retroDirective}. - excerpt는 워드프레스 발췌문(글 목록/공유 시 노출)으로 쓸 1~2문장짜리 짧고 흥미로운 요약을 작성해줘. - meta_description은 본문에는 노출되지 않는 검색엔진용 요약(150자 내외)으로 따로 작성해줘. excerpt와는 톤이 달라도 돼. - category는 정치/경제/사회/생활문화/IT과학/연예/스포츠/국제/기타/본방사수 중 이 포스팅에 가장 맞는 하나로 골라줘. TV 프로그램 방영분·재방송 시청 후기나 실시간 방송 반응처럼 '본방송을 챙겨보는' 성격의 콘텐츠라면 본방사수를 선택해줘. - 소제목(

태그)은 매번 같은 형식('~란?', '~정리' 등) 대신 이번 글마다 다른 톤(질문형, 요약형, 임팩트형 등)으로 만들어줘. - 아래는 SEO 체크리스트야, 반드시 다 지켜줘: 1) title에 이 포스팅의 키워드(${$('Build News Summary').first().json.keyword})를 그대로, 반드시 포함시켜줘 (이 title은 URL과 이미지 대체텍스트에도 그대로 재사용되니 절대 빠뜨리면 안 돼). 2) meta_description에도 이 키워드를 그대로 포함시켜줘. 3) body_html 전체 분량 중 앞부분 10% 이내(즉 첫 문단 근처)에 이 키워드가 최소 한 번 자연스럽게 등장하게 해줘 (도입부 문체는 위 지침대로 하되, 키워드 언급 자체는 빠뜨리지 마). 4) body_html 전체에서 이 키워드가 최소 2~3회 이상 자연스럽게 반복 등장하게 해줘 (억지로 욱여넣지 말고 문맥에 맞게). 5) body_html 안의 소제목(

태그) 중 최소 하나에는 이 키워드를 포함시켜줘. 6) body_html은 최소 600단어 분량(한국어 기준 공백 제외 약 1500자, 공백 포함 약 2000자 이상) 이상으로 충분히 길게 작성해줘 — 너무 짧게 끝내지 마. - body_image_keywords는 본문 중간에 삽입할 사진 2장을 무료 스톡 사진 사이트(Pexels)에서 검색할 때 쓸 영어 키워드 배열이야. 반드시 정확히 2개를 만들어줘, 각각 2~4단어. 이 글이 다루는 서로 다른 두 장면/측면을 표현해줘 (두 이미지가 같은 내용이면 안 됨 -- 예: 하나는 인물/상황, 다른 하나는 배경/장소). 카테고리 수준의 뭉뚱그린 단어 말고 이 기사의 구체적인 소재를 반영해줘. 단, Pexels는 실존 인물 이름이나 한국 고유명사로는 검색이 안 되니, 그런 경우 그 인물/사안이 속한 상황을 묘사하는 일반적인 영어 단어로 바꿔서 표현해줘 (예: '손흥민 부상' -> 'soccer player injury field', '비트코인 급등' -> 'cryptocurrency finance chart growth'). - body_html 안에는 태그나 '[사진: ...]', '(이미지: ...)' 같은 이미지 자리표시·캡션을 절대 넣지 마. 대표 이미지와 본문 이미지 모두 이 워크플로우가 별도로 자동 삽입하니, 본문은 순수 텍스트(문단과 필요한 경우 소제목 정도)로만 작성해줘. - 절대 뉴스 기사를 단순히 요약만 하지 마. 이 사안이 왜 지금 화제인지에 대한 배경, 앞으로 어떻게 흘러갈지에 대한 전망, 비슷한 과거 사례와의 비교, 이게 독자에게 왜 중요한지 같은 너만의 관점과 분석을 본문의 절반 가까운 분량으로 담아줘. 기사 내용을 재배열한 것처럼 읽히면 안 되고, 읽고 나서 뭔가 새로운 통찰을 얻었다는 느낌이 들어야 해.`; const comment = $('Evaluate News Review').first().json.comment; return comment ? base + ` [검토자 코멘트] ${comment} 위 코멘트 내용을 최대한 반영해서 작성해줘.` : base; })() }] }) }}

nodes.name: Claude Draft
nodes.notes: References 'Build News Summary' by name (not $json) because $json here is the Wait node's resumed payload, not the news summary.

nodes.name: Fetch First Article Page
nodes.notes: Fetches the raw HTML of the first news article used for this post, so its og:image meta tag can be reused as BODY IMAGE 1 (not the featured image -- keeping the news outlet's own photo out of the prominently-displayed featured-image slot, and only using it once inline, limits copyright exposure while still honoring the 'one image should be from the article' request). onError=continueRegularOutput + alwaysOutputData=true so a blocked/failed fetch falls through to the Pexels fallback below instead of killing the run. COPYRIGHT NOTE: still reuses a news outlet's own photo for one inline image -- fine for this personal/experimental stage, but reconsider before scaling up or applying for ad monetization.

nodes.name: IF OG Image Found
nodes.notes: true -> use the news article's own og:image as body image 1. false (article fetch blocked/failed, or no og:image tag) -> falls back to a Pexels search (Search Pexels Image B1) instead.

nodes.name: Search Pexels Image
nodes.notes: Featured image search -- runs unconditionally, always Pexels (never the news article's own photo), to keep the prominently-displayed featured-image slot copyright-safe. Uses the first of Claude's body_image_keywords as the search query. VERIFY IN UI: get a free API key at https://www.pexels.com/api/ and paste it into the Authorization header (raw key, no 'Bearer' prefix). alwaysOutputData=true so a zero-result search doesn't skip the rest of the publish chain.

nodes.name: IF Image Found
nodes.notes: false branch (no Pexels result) skips straight to Finalize Featured Media with featured_media left at 0 -- a missing image must never block publishing the post itself.

nodes.name: Upload Featured Image to WordPress
nodes.notes: VERIFY IN UI: reconnect the 'Gabia' Basic Auth credential like the other WordPress nodes. Uploads the downloaded Pexels photo to the media library; response's 'id' becomes the post's featured_media. Always Pexels-sourced, never the news article's own photo -- see 'Search Pexels Image' notes.

nodes.name: Set Featured Image Alt Text
nodes.notes: Side-effect-only leaf node (parallel to Finalize Featured Media, doesn't feed back into the main publish chain) that PATCHes the just-uploaded media item with alt_text so the front-end isn't empty. Uses the post title as alt text since Claude doesn't generate a separate per-image caption. onError=continueRegularOutput so a failure here never blocks publishing.

nodes.name: Search Pexels Image B1
nodes.notes: FALLBACK ONLY for body image 1 -- only runs when the news article had no usable og:image (see IF OG Image Found's false branch). Reuses the first of Claude's body_image_keywords as the search query. alwaysOutputData=true so a zero-result search doesn't block the rest of the publish chain.

nodes.name: IF Image Found B1
nodes.notes: false branch skips straight to Search Pexels Image B2 -- body image 1 failing must never block body image 2 from being attempted, and must never block publishing.

nodes.name: Upload Body Image 1
nodes.notes: VERIFY IN UI: reconnect the 'Gabia' Basic Auth credential. Response's source_url is read by 'Insert Body Images' via $('Upload Body Image 1') -- that lookup throws (caught) if this node never ran, which is how Insert Body Images knows this image is unavailable.

nodes.name: Set Body Image 1 Alt Text
nodes.notes: Side-effect-only leaf node (parallel to Search Pexels Image B2, doesn't feed back into the main publish chain) that PATCHes the just-uploaded media item with alt_text so the front-end isn't empty. Uses the post title as alt text. onError=continueRegularOutput so a failure here never blocks publishing.

nodes.name: Search Pexels Image B2
nodes.notes: Second of the two body_image_keywords Claude generated. Reached from BOTH Upload Body Image 1's success path and IF Image Found B1's false path -- runs regardless of whether body image 1 succeeded.

nodes.name: IF Image Found B2
nodes.notes: false branch skips straight to Insert Body Images -- a missing body image 2 must never block publishing.

nodes.name: Upload Body Image 2
nodes.notes: VERIFY IN UI: reconnect the 'Gabia' Basic Auth credential.

nodes.name: Set Body Image 2 Alt Text
nodes.notes: Side-effect-only leaf node (parallel to Insert Body Images, doesn't feed back into the main publish chain) that PATCHes the just-uploaded media item with alt_text so the front-end isn't empty. Uses the post title as alt text. onError=continueRegularOutput so a failure here never blocks publishing.

nodes.name: Insert Body Images
nodes.notes: Reads Upload Body Image 1/2 via try/catch (same pattern as 'Keyword Context') -- if either node never ran (IF Image Found B1/B2 was false), the lookup throws and that image is simply skipped. Places 1 or 2 images evenly between paragraphs; falls back to a single mid-point insertion if only one image resolved or the article is too short (<3 paragraphs) to space two out meaningfully.

nodes.name: Search WP Category
nodes.notes: VERIFY IN UI: reconnect the 'Gabia' Basic Auth credential (Application Password) -- this and the other new WordPress HTTP nodes all need it reselected after import. The User-Agent header is the confirmed fix for the 401 that blocked auto-publishing -- do not remove it. alwaysOutputData=true (Settings tab) is required: an empty search result ([]) would otherwise make n8n skip every downstream node entirely.

nodes.name: Create WP Category
nodes.notes: Only runs when Search WP Category found no exact match. Creates the category once; future runs with the same category name will find it via search instead.

nodes.name: Get All WP Tags
nodes.notes: Fetches all existing tags once (up to 100) -- matching against Claude's tags array happens in the next Code node, same fetch-all-then-filter pattern used elsewhere in this workflow. Both the 'found' (true) and 'not found' (false) branches of IF Category Found lead here. alwaysOutputData=true (Settings tab) required on a fresh site with zero tags.

nodes.name: Create WP Tag
nodes.notes: Runs once per missing tag (one item per tag from Resolve Tag IDs), creating each new tag in WordPress. neverError=true so a 400 term_exists response (tag actually already existed, just outside Get All WP Tags' first 100 results) lands here as normal data instead of failing the node -- Normalize Created Tag ID picks the existing term's id back out of that error body.

nodes.name: Normalize Created Tag ID
nodes.notes: Create WP Tag has neverError=true, so a term_exists conflict (tag already existed beyond Get All WP Tags' first 100) lands here as {code:'term_exists', data:{term_id}} instead of a thrown error. Reads the tag's real id from whichever shape actually came back (fresh creation vs term_exists conflict) so Aggregate Tag IDs downstream keeps working unmodified.

nodes.name: Aggregate Tag IDs
nodes.notes: Collapses however many items arrived (0 from the false branch's single passthrough item with no id, or N created-tag items from the true branch) into exactly one downstream execution -- avoids Publish WordPress firing multiple times.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ title: $('Parse Claude Response').first().json.title, content: $('Insert Body Images').first().json.body_html, excerpt: $('Parse Claude Response').first().json.excerpt, status: "draft", author: $('Pick Author By Category').first().json.author_id, categories: [(() => { const norm = $('Normalize Category Search').first().json; if (norm.found) return norm.id; try { return $('Create WP Category').first().json.id; } catch (e) { return null; } })()], tags: $('Finalize Tag IDs').first().json.tag_ids, featured_media: $('Finalize Featured Media').first().json.featured_media, meta: { rank_math_focus_keyword: $('Keyword Context').first().json.keyword, rank_math_description: $('Parse Claude Response').first().json.meta_description } }) }}

nodes.name: Publish WordPress
nodes.notes: The User-Agent: curl/8.21.0 header is the confirmed fix for the 401 rest_cannot_create error that blocked this for weeks -- do not remove it. Publishes as status=draft so final polish can be added in wp-admin before actually going live. featured_media comes from the Pexels chain above (0 if no image was found). meta.rank_math_focus_keyword/rank_math_description populate Rank Math's Focus Keyword and SEO meta description fields (previously left at 'Not Set' -- meta_description was already being generated by Claude but was never actually sent to WordPress until now). VERIFY IN UI: if these don't show up in Rank Math after a test post, your Rank Math version may not have 'show_in_rest' enabled for these meta keys -- check Rank Math > Titles & Meta or the plugin's REST API support.

nodes.name: Mark Handled
nodes.notes: Writes to hotnews_candidates -- a table created solely for this workflow. Never trending_keywords.

nodes.name: Check Featured Image Size
nodes.notes: Gabia's WordPress media upload rejects anything over 1500KB. Too-large routes to Finalize Featured Media (no featured image), never blocks publishing.

nodes.name: Check Body Image 1 Size
nodes.notes: News article photos are frequently over Gabia's 1500KB upload cap -- this is what actually failed in live testing (a 1.95MB article photo). Too-large routes to Search Pexels Image B2, the same fallback used for 'no og:image found'.

nodes.name: Check Body Image 2 Size
nodes.notes: Same 1500KB Gabia cap check. Too-large routes to Insert Body Images (skip this image), never blocks publishing.

nodes.name: Pick Post Structure Variant
nodes.notes: Runs in parallel off Build News Summary -- Claude Draft references it by name, same as it already does for Build News Summary/Evaluate News Review.

nodes.name: Pick Author By Category
nodes.notes: The publishing credential (Gabia) stays the same -- it just needs Editor/Administrator role (edit_others_posts capability) to set the 'author' field to a different user, which it already has since it creates categories/tags.

nodes.name: IF Category Unmapped
nodes.notes: true -> a category came back from Claude that isn't in Pick Author By Category's AUTHORS table. The post still publishes fine (under the 기타/이슈랩 fallback), this is just a heads-up to add a real mapping.
